what: Is Blackwell one batch-invariant group? vLLM 0.32.0, VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1, eager, gpt-oss-20b, on a rented RTX 5090 (consumer, South Korea, driver 580.178.04) and a rented RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition (UK, driver 580.173.02), both compute capability 12.0. Each made a determinism run (48 prompts, sequential and 16 concurrent; vllm_determinism.py, reasoning effort low sent at top level) and scored its own run and the home RTX 4090's run in one prefill (vllm_onepass_referee.py). Then the RTX 5090 signed receipts with the llmverify logits processor (vllm_exact_receipts.py generate) and the RTX PRO 6000 checked them in one pass.
determinism: each GPU sequential vs 16 concurrent: 0 of 8,564 positions differ; RTX 5090 vs RTX PRO 6000: 0 replies diverge, 0 of 8,564 positions differ; either vs the home RTX 4090 (Ampere/Ada group): 38 of 48 replies diverge, 2,673 of the 2,712 positions before divergence have different values
onepass_own_run: 0 of 8,564 positions differ on each GPU (3-4 s)
onepass_on_rtx4090_run: top-20 differs at 8,587 of 8,588 positions on each (identical counts on both Blackwell GPUs): a Blackwell referee cannot check an Ada provider
notes: Blackwell (sm_120) is one group across consumer and workstation cards, separate from Ampere/Ada. So with vLLM batch-invariant mode there are at least two exact tiers, each spanning several GPU models; a referee must be in the provider's group.

dgx_spark_gb10.what: The user's DGX Spark (GB10, compute capability 12.1, unified memory), vLLM 0.32.0 in the official arm64 container (vllm/vllm-openai:v0.32.0), VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1, eager, gpu-memory-utilization 0.3 next to other workloads; MXFP4 MoE backend 'HUMMING', TRITON_ATTN attention. Determinism run as on the other GPUs, then one-pass scoring of the GB10's, the RTX 5090's and the home RTX 4090's runs.
dgx_spark_gb10.determinism: sequential vs 16 concurrent: 0 of 8,564 positions differ; GB10 vs RTX 5090: 0 replies diverge, 0 of 8,564 positions differ (so also identical to the RTX PRO 6000)
dgx_spark_gb10.onepass: GB10 scoring its own run and the RTX 5090's: 0 of 8,564 positions differ (18-22 s); the RTX 4090's run: 8,587 of 8,588 differ (other group)

rule_at_more_settings.what: the GB10 with the llmverify logits processor signed receipts at greedy, T=0.2, T=1.5 and T=1.0 with top-k 10 and min-p 0.05 (plus tampered copies) and checked them itself in one pass
rule_at_more_settings.note: one tampered top-k/min-p receipt already fails a client-side check: lowering the winner's committed logprob also moves the min-p threshold, so the edit breaks the rule recomputed from the committed numbers

dgx_spark_gb10.verdict: Blackwell is one exact group from a workstation card to the DGX Spark: RTX 5090, RTX PRO 6000 and GB10 compute the same numbers, so a Spark can referee RTX 5090 / PRO 6000 providers in one pass. The rule is exact at low and high temperatures and with top-k / min-p truncation.
